title: Impact of Minimum Drinking Age on Alcohol Consumption

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)** is the appropriate causal method here. The minimum legal drinking age (MLDA) of 21 creates a sharp cutoff: individuals just below 21 cannot legally purchase alcohol, while those at or above 21 can. The running variable is age (in months, centered or normalized around the cutoff), and treatment is deterministically assigned at the threshold.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **No manipulation of the running variable:** Individuals cannot precisely manipulate their age to sort around the cutoff.
2. **Continuity of potential outcomes:** In the absence of treatment, expected alcohol consumption would be continuous through the age-21 threshold. Any discontinuity at the cutoff is attributable to the MLDA policy.
3. **Local randomization:** Individuals just below and just above 21 are comparable in all respects except legal drinking access.

The `running_var` appears normalized (values between 0 and 1, with 0.5 likely representing the cutoff based on `treated` and `near_cutoff` patterns). I will verify the cutoff location empirically.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load required libraries
if (!require("rdrobust")) install.packages("rdrobust", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
if (!require("rddensity")) install.packages("rddensity", repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)

# ============================================================
# Read data
# ============================================================
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s95_data.csv")
cat("Dimensions:", dim(df), "\n")
cat("Summary of running variable:\n")
print(summary(df$running_var))
cat("\nSummary of treated:\n")
print(table(df$treated))

# ============================================================
# Identify the cutoff
# ============================================================
# Find the cutoff: the minimum running_var value among treated
cutoff_candidates <- c(0.5, 0.25)
# Empirical check: min of treated and max of untreated
min_treated <- min(df$running_var[df$treated == 1])
max_untreated <- max(df$running_var[df$treated == 0])
cat("\nMin running_var among treated:", min_treated, "\n")
cat("Max running_var among untreated:", max_untreated, "\n")
cutoff <- (min_treated + max_untreated) / 2
cat("Estimated cutoff:", cutoff, "\n")

# Use a round cutoff if it falls close
if (abs(cutoff - 0.5) < 0.05) cutoff <- 0.5
if (abs(cutoff - 0.25) < 0.05) cutoff <- 0.25
cat("Using cutoff:", cutoff, "\n\n")

# Center the running variable at the cutoff
df$X <- df$running_var - cutoff

# ============================================================
# 1. MAIN ANALYSIS: rdrobust (local polynomial RDD)
# ============================================================
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("MAIN ANALYSIS: rdrobust with MSE-optimal bandwidth\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")

rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0)
summary(rd_main)

cat("\n>>> LATE (Local Average Treatment Effect) at cutoff:", 
    round(rd_main$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat(">>> Robust p-value:", round(rd_main$pv[3], 4), "\n")
cat(">>> Robust 95% CI: [", round(rd_main$ci[3,1], 4), ",", 
    round(rd_main$ci[3,2], 4), "]\n")
cat(">>> Optimal bandwidth (h):", round(rd_main$bws[1,1], 4), "\n\n")

# ============================================================
# 2. PARAMETRIC RDD: Linear regression with different bandwidths
# ============================================================
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("PARAMETRIC RDD ESTIMATES\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")

# Full sample
lm_full <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = df)
cat("Full sample - Linear interaction model:\n")
cat("  Treatment effect:", round(coef(lm_full)["treated"], 4), 
    " (SE:", round(summary(lm_full)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"], 4), 
    ", p:", round(summary(lm_full)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), ")\n\n")

# Restrict to optimal bandwidth from rdrobust
h_opt <- rd_main$bws[1,1]
df_bw <- df[abs(df$X) <= h_opt, ]
cat("Observations within optimal bandwidth (h=", round(h_opt, 4), "):", nrow(df_bw), "\n")

lm_opt <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = df_bw)
cat("Optimal bandwidth - Linear interaction model:\n")
cat("  Treatment effect:", round(coef(lm_opt)["treated"], 4),
    " (SE:", round(summary(lm_opt)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"], 4),
    ", p:", round(summary(lm_opt)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), ")\n\n")

# Quadratic specification (full sample)
lm_quad <- lm(y ~ treated * X + treated * I(X^2), data = df)
cat("Full sample - Quadratic interaction model:\n")
cat("  Treatment effect:", round(coef(lm_quad)["treated"], 4),
    " (SE:", round(summary(lm_quad)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"], 4),
    ", p:", round(summary(lm_quad)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"], 4), ")\n\n")

# ============================================================
# 3. ROBUSTNESS: Varying bandwidths
# ============================================================
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("ROBUSTNESS: Sensitivity to bandwidth choice\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")

bandwidths <- c(h_opt * 0.5, h_opt * 0.75, h_opt, h_opt * 1.25, h_opt * 1.5)
cat(sprintf("%-12s %-12s %-12s %-12s %-8s\n", "Bandwidth", "Estimate", "Std.Error", "p-value", "N"))

for (h in bandwidths) {
  df_h <- df[abs(df$X) <= h, ]
  if (nrow(df_h) > 10) {
    fit_h <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = df_h)
    est <- coef(fit_h)["treated"]
    se <- summary(fit_h)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"]
    pv <- summary(fit_h)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"]
    cat(sprintf("%-12.4f %-12.4f %-12.4f %-12.4f %-8d\n", h, est, se, pv, nrow(df_h)))
  }
}

# ============================================================
# 4. ROBUSTNESS: rdrobust with different kernel/polynomial
# ============================================================
cat("\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("ROBUSTNESS: Alternative rdrobust specifications\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")

# Triangular kernel (default), uniform kernel, epanechnikov
for (kern in c("triangular", "uniform", "epanechnikov")) {
  rd_k <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, kernel = kern)
  cat(sprintf("Kernel: %-15s  Estimate: %7.4f  Robust p: %6.4f  h: %6.4f\n",
              kern, rd_k$coef[1], rd_k$pv[3], rd_k$bws[1,1]))
}

# Higher-order polynomial
cat("\n")
for (p in c(1, 2, 3)) {
  rd_p <- tryCatch({
    rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$X, c = 0, p = p)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(rd_p)) {
    cat(sprintf("Polynomial order: %d  Estimate: %7.4f  Robust p: %6.4f  h: %6.4f\n",
                p, rd_p$coef[1], rd_p$pv[3], rd_p$bws[1,1]))
  }
}

# ============================================================
# 5. VALIDITY: McCrary density test
# ============================================================
cat("\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("VALIDITY CHECK: McCrary density test (rddensity)\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")

dens_test <- rddensity(X = df$X, c = 0)
cat("T-statistic:", round(dens_test$test$t_jk, 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(dens_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")
if (dens_test$test$p_jk > 0.05) {
  cat("=> No evidence of manipulation at the cutoff (good!)\n")
} else {
  cat("=> Warning: Evidence of density discontinuity at cutoff\n")
}

# ============================================================
# 6. VISUALIZATION
# ============================================================
cat("\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("VISUAL: Binned scatter plot\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")

# Create bins for visualization
n_bins <- 20
df$bin <- cut(df$X, breaks = n_bins)
bin_means <- aggregate(y ~ bin + treated, data = df, FUN = mean)
cat("Binned means computed for", n_bins, "bins\n")

# Simple visual summary: means on each side near cutoff
near_left <- df[df$X >= -0.05 & df$X < 0, ]
near_right <- df[df$X >= 0 & df$X <= 0.05, ]
cat("\nMean Y just below cutoff (within 0.05):", round(mean(near_left$y), 4), 
    " (N=", nrow(near_left), ")\n")
cat("Mean Y just above cutoff (within 0.05):", round(mean(near_right$y), 4), 
    " (N=", nrow(near_right), ")\n")
cat("Raw difference:", round(mean(near_right$y) - mean(near_left$y), 4), "\n")

# ============================================================
# SUMMARY
# ============================================================
cat("\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n")
cat("SUMMARY OF MAIN RESULT\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 60), "\n\n")
cat("The RDD estimate of the effect of reaching the legal drinking\n")
cat("age (21) on alcohol consumption is:\n\n")
cat("  LATE =", round(rd_main$coef[1], 4), "\n")
cat("  Robust 95% CI: [", round(rd_main$ci[3,1], 4), ",", 
    round(rd_main$ci[3,2], 4), "]\n")
cat("  Robust p-value:", round(rd_main$pv[3], 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive.** Reaching the legal drinking age of 21 should cause an increase in alcohol consumption, as individuals gain legal access to purchase alcohol.

**Expected magnitude:** Based on the data preview, the outcome variable `y` appears to be on a relatively small scale (values near 0-0.6). Looking at the preview:
- Treated individuals (running_var > cutoff) show y values around 0.4-0.6
- Untreated individuals show y values near 0 (-0.04 to 0.2)

I expect the discontinuity at the cutoff to be approximately **0.3 to 0.5 units**, which would be both economically and statistically significant. The `near_cutoff` variable in the data suggests the researchers anticipated using observations close to the threshold, consistent with a local RDD approach.

**Robustness expectations:**
- The estimate should remain positive and significant across different bandwidths and polynomial orders, though precision may decrease with narrower bandwidths.
- The McCrary density test should show no evidence of manipulation (people cannot choose their exact birthday relative to the policy cutoff).
- The treatment effect should be stable across kernel choices (triangular, uniform, epanechnikov), lending credibility to the finding that legal access increases consumption at the extensive and/or intensive margin.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: The identification strategy leverages the age-21 drinking age cutoff as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Reaching the age of 21 leads to an increase in alcohol consumption.
